CAUSES OF AN ACUTE 
COPD EXACERBATION 
 
* Infections (viral, bacterial) 
* Pulmonary embolism 
* Pneumothorax 
* Pneumonia 
* Cardiac failure 
* Pericardial effusion 
* Lobar atelectasis  
* Anaphylaxis 
* Air pollution 
* Non-compliance 
* Iatrogenic

Contents

COPD ED MANAGEMENT 
CRITERIA FOR NON-INVASIVE VENTILATORY SUPPORT 
One or more of the following may be present 
 
* Moderate to severe dyspnoea with use of accessory muscles and    
   paradoxical abdominal motion 
* Respiratory rate 25 bpm 
* Moderate to severe acidosis à pH < 7.35 
* Hypercapnia à PaCO2 > 45 mmHg 
 
**Refer to NIV protocol** 
INTUBATED PATIENT CONSIDERATIONS 
* Ventilator Settings 
 
MODE   
Volume Assist Control 
 
TV 
 
6ml/kg (4-6ml/kg) 
 
I:E ratio 
1:3 (may increase to 1:4 or 1:5 as needed) 
 
RR 
 
10 -12 bpm 
 
Alarm Pmax 
Readjust to allow for higher pressures initially 
* Preload with 20ml/kg IV fluids to avoid a precipitous drop in BP  
* Continue with inline nebulisation 
IF DETERIORATION AFTER INTUBATION CONSIDER 
* Displacement of ET tube  
* Obstruction of ET tube / mucous plug 
* Pneumothorax / pneumomediastinum 
* Equipment failure / disconnection 
* Suctioning required / stomach overdistension 
INDICATIONS FOR ADMISSION 
 
* Moderate to severe exacerbations 
* Worsening hypercarbia with acute respiratory acidosis (pH < 7.30) 
* Altered mentation 
* Severe underlying COPD, severe comorbidities or old age 
* Poorly controlled psychiatric patient 
* Inadequate response to treatment  
* Patient on oral steroids prior to exacerbation 
* Lack of home support
